title: Beyond Local Berry Geometry: A First-Principles Finite-Momentum Theory of Electronic Position
summary: Electronic position controls how a crystal polarizes and responds to an external field. In crystals, it is usually described through local changes of electronic states in momentum space. This Berry framework has reshaped modern solid-state physics, but strong fields drive electrons across a finite momentum range, where coherence between different momenta becomes part of the response. Here we establish a first-principles theory of electronic position at finite momentum that retains this missing information.
